'''Dervilla Maura Xavier Donnelly''' (1930 – 14 November 2024) was an Irish chemist who was Professor of Phytochemistry at [[University College Dublin]]. She was the first woman to receive the [[Cunningham Medal]] from the [[Royal Irish Academy]] and was recognised by WITS ([[Women in Technology and Science]]) with their inaugural Lifetime Achievement award.

==Early life and education==
Dervilla Maura Xavier Donnelly was born in [[Dublin]] in 1930.<ref>{{cite news |title=Dubliner receives Boyle Medal for Scientific Excellence |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/dubliner-receives-boyle-medal-for-scientific-excellence-1.508078 |newspaper=The Irish Times |accessdate=11 February 2019 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Portrait of Professor Dervilla Donnelly |url=https://www.ucd.ie/chem/about/portraitofprofessordervilladonnelly/ |access-date=15 November 2024 |website=UCD School Of Chemistry}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Höss |first=Werner |date=20 November 2001 |others=Layout by R.K Kowanz. Printed by Paul Gerin. |title=Annual Report 2001 |url=https://forwit.at/archive/files/rat-fte-pdf-en/documents/annual_reports/Annual%2520Report%25202001.pdf |access-date=15 November 2024 |website={{Ill|Rat für Forschung und Technologieentwicklung|lt=Austrian Council for Sciences, Technology, and Innovation|de}} |page=10 }}</ref> She studied chemistry at [[University College Dublin]] as an undergraduate and went on to complete her PhD there under the supervision of T. S. Wheeler. She pursued postdoctoral studies at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]].<ref name=":0" />

==Academic career==
Donnelly was appointed lecturer in chemistry at UCD in 1956, where she specialised in [[Phytochemistry]]. She was appointed Professor of Phytochemistry in 1979.<ref name=":0" /> Her research in the area of wood chemistry was of particular interest to the forestry industry in Ireland and she was able to apply her findings to a number of complex problems in Irish forestry. She also developed international collaborations with researchers in France. During her academic career she supervised more than 80 PhD students.<ref name=":1" />

==Appointments==
Donnelly was elected to membership of The [[Royal Irish Academy]] 1968 and she served three times as vice-president of the academy.<ref name=":2" /> She was president of the [[Institute of Chemistry of Ireland]] from 1994 to 1996.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guiry |first=Pat |date=16 June 2015 |title=Dervilla Donnelly |url=https://www.ucd.ie/president/about/universityawards/honorarydegrees/2015/dervilladonnelly/ |access-date=15 November 2024 |website=UCD President's Office}}</ref>

In December 1989, Dervilla Donnelly was elected the first woman President of the [[Royal Dublin Society]], a position she held for three years.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Looking forward to new ideas: Professor Dervilla Donnelly, the first woman president of the Royal Dublin Society, talks about the work of the society and her hopes for the future|date=16 July 1990|newspaper=The Irish Times}}</ref> She was the first woman elected to the position after 258 years of male presidents. She had been involved in the RDS since the 1960s, was elected to the science committee in 1976 and to the council in 1985. She succeeded [[Francis O'Reilly]] as president, who also nominated her as his successor.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Making her space in the male world of the RDS|last=MacConnell|first=Seán|date=14 July 1990|newspaper=The Irish Times}}</ref>

In 1995, she was appointed chair of the council of the [[Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies]], by [[Niamh Bhreathnach|Niamh Bhreathneach]] who was Minister for Education at the time.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://oireachtasdebates.oireachtas.ie/debates%20authoring/debateswebpack.nsf/takes/dail1996022000148?opendocument|title=Parliamentary Debates|date=20 February 1996|website=oireachtasdebates.oireachtas.ie|access-date=25 July 2017}}</ref> She retained this appointment for 15 years until 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 February 2017 |title=RIA Cunningham Medal for Prof Dervilla Donnelly |url=https://www.ucd.ie/newsandopinion/news/2017/feb/24/riacunninghammedalforprofdervilladonnelly/ |access-date=15 November 2024 |website=UCD}}</ref>

==Later life and death==
In 2012, Donnelly was one of five "inspiring women" interviewed for a video made by WITS. ''Inspiring Women Interviews'' was launched on [[International Women's Day]] at the European Parliament office in Dublin. It aims to encourage 16+ year old girls to consider careers in [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.siliconrepublic.com/innovation/women-in-technology-inspire-students-about-scientific-careers|title=Women in technology inspire students about scientific careers|date=8 March 2012|work=Siliconrepublic.com|access-date=20 July 2017}}</ref>

Donnelly was listed as one of 100 top women in science, technology, engineering and maths by ''[[Silicon Republic]]'' as part of their Women Invent Tomorrow campaign in March 2014.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.siliconrepublic.com/careers/women-invent-100-top-women-in-science-technology-engineering-and-maths-part-1|title=Women Invent: 100 top women in science, technology, engineering and maths – Part 1|date=11 March 2014|work=Siliconrepublic.com|access-date=20 July 2017}}</ref>

Donnelly died at [[St. James's Hospital]] on 14 November 2024, at the age of 94.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gleeson |first=Colin |date=14 November 2024 |title=Renowned Irish scientist Dervilla Donnelly dies aged 94 |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/ireland/2024/11/14/renowned-irish-scientist-dervilla-donnelly-dies-aged-94/ |access-date=15 November 2024 |newspaper=[[The Irish Times]]}}</ref>

==Awards==
Donnelly was awarded UCD's Charter Day medal in December 2000, for her contribution to the country and the university.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/ucd-award-for-retired-professor-1.1119007|title=UCD award for retired professor|date=2 December 2000|newspaper=The Irish Times|access-date=19 July 2017}}</ref> In the same year she received the Boyle-Higgins gold medal award from the [[Institute of Chemistry of Ireland]], awarded for "an outstanding and internationally recognised research contribution to the advancement of chemistry".<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chemistryireland.org/html/awards.html|title=Institute Awards|website=Institute of Chemistry of Ireland|access-date=19 July 2017|archive-date=21 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171021131839/http://www.chemistryireland.org/html/awards.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The Women in Science and Technology (WITS) inaugural Lifetime Achievement award was presented to Professor Donnelly in June 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://witsireland.com/activities/lifetime-achievement-awards/|title=Lifetime Achievement Awards|publisher=WITS|access-date=19 July 2017}}</ref>

In 2017 Professor Donnelly became the first woman to receive the [[Royal Irish Academy]]'s highest honour, the [[Cunningham Medal]], which recognises "outstanding contributions to scholarship and the objectives of the Academy".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.ucd.ie/newsandopinion/news/2017/feb/24/riacunninhammedalforprofdervilladonnelly/|title=Professor Dervilla Donnelly first woman to receive Royal Irish Academy's highest honour|date=24 February 2017|website=University College Dublin|access-date=19 July 2017}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/science/irish-chemist-to-receive-highest-honour-from-ria-1.2979649|title=Irish Chemist to receive highest honour from RIA|date=23 February 2017|newspaper=The Irish Times|access-date=19 July 2017}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/business/innovation/leading-irish-scientist-honoured-by-royal-irish-academy-1.3001555|title=Leading Irish scientist honoured by Royal Irish Academy|date=7 March 2017|newspaper=The Irish Times|access-date=19 July 2017}}</ref>
